issue_context.title: `ClientClusterManifestProvider` can block host shutdown
issue_context.body:
- We've occasionally had our Orleans client application continue running even though the `IHost` has been stopped.
- Observed after updating to 8.2, though it may not be directly connected to that update.
- Specifically, the main thread has a call to `host.WaitForShutdownAsync` while a different thread calls `host.StopAsync`.
- I can see in the logs the start of the typical shutdown sequence including getting to `Client shutdown completed`; however, things keep running after that point.
- I can see ongoing logs from the `ClientClusterManifestProvider` about failures trying to obtain the cluster manifest (because the runtime client has been disposed).

From @ledjon-behluli:

> yeah that component relies on being disposed to shutdown, and might not align with the runtime client's shutdown timing.
> i think having an explicit StopAsync, or at lease manually invoking DisposeAsync on the manifest provider when the outsideRuntimeClient is stopped would be a good idea
> It (the provider) being a singleton stops an effective disposing (thereby stopping) by the dotnet runtime when the runtime client is stopped
